subject: sociology
title: Theory & Methods: Structure, Agency & Sociology as Science
welcome_lead: Are we shaped by structure, or do we make it? Giddens says both.
meta_desc: A-Level Sociology theory structure agency Giddens structuration sociology science.
final_note: Society makes us; we make society — at the same time.

concepts.def: Capacity of individuals to act independently.
Giddens — structure and agency mutually constituted.
Structure both medium and outcome of action.
Weber — research should not be skewed by personal values.
Researcher and society both watch and adjust.

walkthroughs.body_html: Giddens (1984): structure and agency are two sides of one process. Structures (rules and resources) shape action; action reproduces (or transforms) structure. Example: speaking English uses grammar (structure) but each utterance reproduces it.

Bourdieu (1977): habitus — dispositions internalised from social position that produce practice. Field: arenas (art, education) where actors compete using capital (cultural, social, economic). Structure operates through bodies and tastes.

Positivists say yes — use scientific method. Interpretivists say no — social action is meaningful. Popper (1959): science requires falsifiability — much sociology fails. Kuhn (1962): science is paradigm-based — sociology has multiple paradigms simultaneously. Realism: sociology can be science if it uncovers underlying structures.
